newsitem.title: USA: Wabash National asset bid a smart move - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Wabash National asset bid a smart move - analysts.

text.p: Wabash National Corp, which plans to bid on Fruehauf Trailer Corp's assets, will gain access to previously underserved markets and reap other benefits if the deal closes, industry analysts said.

"Wabash currently has some distribution programs for non-fleet buyers and this deal puts them in a position to capture a larger share of that market," Leon Dodge, an analyst at GS2 Securities Inc, said Wednesday.
Wabash said earlier it reached an expense reimbursement agreement with Fruehauf. Bids will be turned in Friday.

Wabash, a manufacturer of standard and custom truck trailers, hopes to buy the bankrupt competitor's 31-branch sales and distribution network, a manufacturing facility in Scott County, Tennessee and certain intellectual property, a company spokeswoman told Reuters.
Fruehauf's manufacturing plants in Mexico and Ft. Madison, Iowa, are not part of the Wabash proposal, Wabash said.
The current court schedule calls for bids to be submitted Friday, the auction Monday and a court ruling on the bids on March 20, the spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman declined to say how much Wabash would bid for the assets, although the company said earlier it will receive $1.5 million and other expenses if the court accepts any other offer.
Fruehauf filed for Chapter 11 protection in October.
"The market seems to be saying that this may not be a good deal, but I think it's a good fit," Darren Bagwell, an analyst at Robert W. Baird & Co Inc, said.
"Wabash has been looking to do this for some time," Bagwell said. "(The distribution network) was always profitable for Fruehauf, even in the bad times."
Christopher Mecray, an analyst at Alex. Brown, agreed the deal is a smart strategic move for Wabash.
"Wabash has a limited presence in the retail market because of a lack of a distribution network," he said.
"Wabash can immediately add between $80 million and $90 million in parts," Mecray said, "and since one out of every five trailers on the road is a Fruehauf, there's a strong customer base out there."
Mecray said his initial guess was that Wabash would see an earnings benefit of $0.05 and $0.10 a share in 1998.
"It could be more," he said, "but I see modest accretive impact for the next year or year-and-a-half."
The company declined to comment on Mecray's projection.
Wabash National reported earnings of $3.6 million, or $0.19 a share, for fiscal 1996.
Its shares were off 1/4 Wednesday at 15-3/4.
